title: Ordinary coefficient square for compactification exchange
statement: Fix l,E,o,a, a base B, an input family X and ordinary integral inputs K [def-sf-integral-realization-assembly-data]. For compactifications cf of f:U→V and cfprime of fprime:Uprime→Vprime, and a compatible map x,y,z of their open/proper diagrams with cartesian open square, the explicit ordinary coefficient map [def-sf-integral-ordinary-expression-reduction] of pull_y(compactSupport_cf(e)), followed by the prescribed system compactification exchange, equals reduction of the prescribed ringed compactification exchange followed by the coefficient of compactSupport_cfprime(pull_x(e)). This is only exchange; no tensor or projection compatibility is asserted. The fixed maps are not replaced by chosen maps.

source.place: The maps used here are tensor reassociation, evaluation, and adjunction units and counits, whose coefficient comparisons are proved in lem-fix-operation-reduction; coherence inherited from individual maps.

proof.text: First prove the forward pullback coefficient boundary from pull_square_nat by reversing the square. Transpose this boundary through the actual proper adjunctions using the generic matePastingSquare lemma; naturality inserts an arbitrary coefficient map. For the open part, fixedOpenReduction_isIso and the inverse-mate unit equation give the open beta coefficient square by inverse cancellation. Identify the prescribed system and ringed compactification transformations with their associator composites by reflexivity at the whole-transformation level. The generic compactCompositeSquare takes components only in abstract categories and uses pasteCoefficientSquare to paste the proper exchange square, the open beta square, and naturality of the proper reduction mate on arbitrary coefficient objects. Specialize the resulting compactificationCoefficientOnObjects identity to the ringed interpretation of e and its ordinaryReduction arrow. The endpoints are definitionally the displayed ordinary coefficient maps; no ordinaryBasicSquare or completion theorem is used. Infer the specialized categorical function type before supplying the proper and open square proofs. Explicit structural congruence, functor component equations and proof irrelevance transport those proofs to its premises and its result to the normalized statement. This proof-generation normalization follows the existing private method in IntegralOrdinaryProperOpenSquare and all generated congruence proofs are checked by the kernel.

proof_origin.place: C7 forced cycle repair: independently paste proper exchange, open beta and proper reduction naturality in abstract categories, then specialize exactly.

lean.statement:
theorem ordinaryCompactificationExchangeSquare
    (o : Operations l E) (a : AmbientModels l E o)
    {B : Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u} {X : I → Over B}
    (K : ∀ i, Integral l E (X i).left)
    {U V U' V' : Over B}
    (f : U ⟶ V) (f' : U' ⟶ V') (cf : Compactification f.left)
    (cf' : Compactification f'.left) (x : U' ⟶ U) (y : V' ⟶ V) (z : cf'.Z ⟶ cf.Z)
    (wi : x.left ≫ cf.i = cf'.i ≫ z) (wp : z ≫ cf.g = cf'.g ≫ y.left)
    (hi : IsPullback x.left cf'.i cf.i z) (e : Expression B I X U) :
    (Expression.pull y (.compactSupport f cf e)).ordinaryReduction l E o a K ≫
        (compactificationExchange l E o a.compositors a.openComparisons
          cf cf' x.left y.left z wi wp hi).app
            (e.systemObj l E o ((inputReduction l E X).obj K)) =
      (calculus l E V'.left).reduction.map
          ((ringedCompactificationExchange l E a.ringedModels a.ringedOpenComparisons
            cf cf' x.left y.left z wi wp hi).app (e.ringedObj l E a.ringedModels K)) ≫
        (Expression.compactSupport f' cf' (.pull x e)).ordinaryReduction l E o a K
